work_completed: Study of text editing with Avalonia on Android (docs/architecture/editor-de-texto-avalonia.md): Avalonia 12.1.3 Android input path read in source (AndroidInputMethod, AvaloniaInputConnection, TextEditBuffer, EditCommand, InputMethodManager, TextInputOptions, TextBoxTextInputMethodClient, FocusManager), AvaloniaEdit's TextAreaTextInputMethodClient, community reports, Lunet and Numa code and the owner's reports; rules R1-R8 for any Avalonia text field.

Confirmed causes: multi-line fields are declared Done (Enter hides the keyboard) because neither TextBox nor AvaloniaEdit sets TextInputOptions.Multiline; AvaloniaEdit's IME client reports a 1-based column as the selection index and ignores selection sets without a selection (composition doubles/deletes letters: 'var yye = 1;'), never asks for the keyboard on tap; Avalonia only asks with SHOW_IMPLICIT; Lunet re-parented the editor (first tap / find / menu), hid the AI sheet when the keyboard opened, re-parented the AI input and let its buttons take focus, and dropped focus on workspace rebuilds.

Fixes in Lunet: CodeInputClient replaces AvaloniaEdit's client (0-based window of whole lines anchored around the caret, working selection set, tap request, context menu actions, reset on load); code editor multi-line, Return, no suggestions; global style declares every AcceptsReturn TextBox multi-line; explicit keyboard request on a tap on the focused field (ShowSoftInput flags 0, posted); DocumentEditor keeps a fixed frame (editor and code bar never re-parented); the support sheet stays when its field has focus; AI composer built once with non-focusable buttons; WorkspaceView.Rebuild gives focus back within the same tab and panel.

AndroidImeSimulator: line-by-line port of Avalonia 12.1.3's Android TextEditBuffer/EditCommand driven through the headless window; also proves AvaloniaEdit's own bridge still has the bugs (the test fails when a future AvaloniaEdit fixes them).

verification.check: EditorKeyboardTests (15 tests: Enter, caret, composition, accents, delete, keyboard selection, long-file window, tap request, reset, code bar without re-parenting, rebuild keeps focus, AI sheet focus and keyboard, multi-line fields)

known_issues: Not tested on a phone: Gboard and Samsung keyboard behaviour (when they compose or commit) is not modelled by the simulator; the device checklist is section 7 of the study.
Numa (Urbe C#) still has multi-line fields without TextInputOptions.Multiline (OCR, agent questions, agent prompts and instructions); recorded as a recommendation in the study, not changed here.
